entries.name: Ackee and saltfish
entries.note: Grace publishes a canned-ackee preparation with saltfish, garlic and Scotch bonnet. This does not authenticate the archived 300 g cod formula.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 1 can (540 g) drained commercially processed ackee
300 g salted cod, desalted and flaked

ingredients: 1 teaspoon Grace Caribbean Traditions black pepper
1 can Grace ackee in brine, drained
steps: Soak the saltfish in cold water for about an hour. Discard that water, add fresh water and cook the fish until tender. Remove bones and flake it.
Sauté the onion, garlic, escallion, tomato and both peppers in the oil. Add the fish, drained canned ackee and black pepper.
Combine gently, cover and leave over low heat for about two minutes.
publishedPreparation.status: Documented source transcription; not kitchen-tested by Tony’s Guide
publishedPreparation.treatment: Source ingredient quantities preserved; directions paraphrased. No conversions or substitutions.
publishedPreparation.limitation: The source uses commercially canned ackee. Can size is not specified; do not invent a gram conversion.

entries.name: Callaloo and saltfish
entries.note: Lesa documents fresh callaloo with desalted cod. Her quantities and the archived formulation differ; callaloo names also differ across Caribbean islands.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 180 g salted cod, desalted and flaked

entries.name: Fried dumplings
entries.note: Lesa documents flour dumplings fried in oil, with optional butter. Keep this separate from sweet cornmeal festival.

entries.name: Festival
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham publishes a flour-and-cornmeal festival with milk, butter and optional nutmeg. Attribute this version to him rather than treating its proportions as universal.

entries.name: Rice and peas
entries.note: Grace uses canned kidney beans and coconut milk. The archived draft starts with dried beans; those procedures are not interchangeable.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 200 g dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and safely boiled

steps: Bring the coconut milk and water to a boil in a three-litre pot. Stir in the escallion, onion, thyme, canned beans and salt.
Add the rice and whole pepper. Cover and return to a boil, then lower the heat and cook until the rice is tender.
Keep the pepper intact when stirring.
publishedPreparation.status: Documented source transcription; not kitchen-tested by Tony’s Guide
publishedPreparation.treatment: Source ingredient quantities preserved; directions paraphrased. No conversions or substitutions.
publishedPreparation.limitation: This is Grace’s canned-bean version. The source does not specify rice variety, can weight or a rinsing/draining instruction; no conversions or dried-bean substitution are supplied.

entries.name: Brown stew chicken
entries.note: Lesa describes browning chicken before simmering it with vegetables and sauce. The source supports her preparation, not the archived proportions.

entries.name: Curry goat
entries.note: Grace documents a goat curry with a refrigerated marinade and searing stage. Tenderness and cooking duration depend on the cut.

entries.name: Stew peas
entries.note: Grace “Grandma” Reynolds publishes stew peas with salted and stewing meats, coconut milk and spinners. A meatless version requires separate attribution.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 250 g dried kidney beans, soaked and safely boiled

entries.name: Escovitch fish
entries.note: Grace documents fried fish served with escovitch sauce, and explicitly names bammy or festival as accompaniments. Its sauce is a separate preparation.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 800 g cleaned snapper or firm fish

entries.name: Mackerel rundown
entries.note: Lesa distinguishes salted-mackerel rundown from an ordinary fish stew and discusses coconut reduction. Preserve that distinction when comparing methods.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 500 g fresh mackerel fillets or properly desalted mackerel

entries.name: Sweet potato pudding
entries.note: Winsome Murphy publishes sweet potato pudding with flour, coconut milk and raisins. This is one published version, not a validated replacement for the archived draft.

entries.name: Sorrel drink
entries.note: Lesa documents sorrel with ginger and spices and discusses versions with and without rum and wine. Alcohol must be disclosed when present.

entries.name: Cornmeal porridge
entries.note: Lesa publishes a coconut-milk cornmeal porridge. Milk choices and sweetening belong to the named preparation.

entries.name: Saltfish fritters
entries.note: Jamaican chef Joan Lue identifies stamp and go as saltfish fritters. Her recipe is a source for both names; the two archive records are not two distinct traditions.

entries.name: Bammy
entries.note: Grace documents grating, pressing and griddle cooking cassava. This is documentary evidence, not a validated detoxification protocol for an unidentified cassava variety.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 500 g commercially prepared, food-safe grated cassava

entries.name: Roast breadfruit
entries.note: Winsome Murphy describes roasting a whole breadfruit and serving it in pieces. No invented fixed roasting time is added here.

entries.name: Coconut rice
entries.note: Lesa publishes coconut rice as a Jamaican preparation. It should not be confused with rice and peas, which contains beans or peas.

entries.name: Jerk chicken
entries.note: Xavier Murphy publishes a jerk-chicken preparation using a separately supplied jerk seasoning. This documents a present-day version, not a historic Maroon spice formula.

entries.name: Curried chicken
entries.note: Grace publishes curried chicken and identifies optional carrot and potato additions. Those options belong to this source, rather than to a claimed national rule.

entries.name: Ital vegetable stew
entries.note: Charla publishes an Ital vegetable stew with ground provisions. It is the same source family as the Ital stew record below, not a separate parish tradition.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 200 g callaloo or washed leafy greens

entries.name: Steamed snapper
entries.note: Fancy’s preparation on Grace uses snapper, stock, vegetables and crackers. The source supports this named version without establishing a parish origin.

entries.name: Pepper shrimp
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham’s peppered shrimp boil includes potatoes and corn. It is a named contemporary variation, not a reconstruction of every Middle Quarters vendor’s method.

entries.name: Banana fritters
entries.note: Lesa publishes banana fritters using ripe bananas and flour. Her egg-free preparation is attributed to her; no claim is made that every household excludes eggs.

entries.name: Ginger beer
entries.note: Lesa publishes a ginger drink with lime and sweetening. This is not evidence of a fermented beverage or of a safe fermentation procedure.

entries.name: Hominy corn porridge
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham uses hominy with a cream-of-wheat and flour thickener, and discusses alternatives. Preserve that specific variation.

entries.name: Green banana porridge
entries.note: Lesa documents porridge made with green bananas and coconut milk. This is different from a ripe-banana fritter batter.

entries.name: Plantain porridge
entries.note: Lesa documents green-plantain porridge. The recipe supports this preparation without dating its invention.

entries.name: Peanut porridge
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham publishes peanut porridge with oatmeal. The page lists vanilla twice in different amounts; clarification is required before reproducing its formula.

entries.name: Oats porridge
entries.note: Grace publishes an oats porridge with dairy, spices and optional raisins. Its larger batch does not validate the smaller archived formula.

steps: Bring eight cups of the water to a boil with evaporated milk, cinnamon leaf, optional raisins and salt.
Mix the oats, nutmeg and cinnamon powder. Combine vanilla with the remaining two cups of water, then stir that liquid into the oats.
Stir the oat mixture into the boiling liquid. When it boils again, reduce the heat and cook for about five minutes. Stir in the condensed milk and serve hot.
publishedPreparation.status: Documented source transcription; not kitchen-tested by Tony’s Guide
publishedPreparation.treatment: Source ingredient quantities preserved; directions paraphrased. No conversions or substitutions.
publishedPreparation.limitation: The published ingredient list says one nutmeg, not one teaspoon. That quantity is retained as a source record and needs clarification and a kitchen trial before adopting this as a Tony’s Guide formula.

entries.name: Stamp and go
entries.note: Joan Lue explicitly calls stamp and go a saltfish fritter. Keep the name as an alias and preserve the duplicate record for audit.

entries.name: Callaloo omelette
entries.note: The Jamaica Tourist Board names a callaloo omelette at Smurfs Café, Treasure Beach, in a 2018 feature. That establishes a menu item at that date, not the café’s recipe or current availability.

entries.name: Steamed cabbage breakfast
entries.note: Lesa documents steamed cabbage and its accompaniments. “Breakfast” is a serving context, not proof of a distinct cabbage formula.

entries.name: Boiled green banana
entries.note: Grace publishes a boiled green-banana preparation. The source quantities and the archived mixed-seasoning version are not certified equivalent.

entries.name: Boiled yam and dumpling
entries.note: Lesa’s hard-food guide documents a combined pot of ground provisions and dumplings. Do not count every combination as a separate inherited recipe.

entries.name: Pumpkin rice
entries.note: Lesa distinguishes plain pumpkin rice from a more seasoned family version. The family account is attributed to her rather than generalized to a parish.

entries.name: Curried shrimp
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham publishes spicy curried shrimp with coconut milk. It is a named cook’s variation.

entries.name: Stewed lentils
entries.note: Grace publishes lentil stew served with pasta and cheese. This establishes a contemporary corporate preparation, not an ancient or necessarily Ital tradition.

entries.name: Coconut shrimp
entries.note: Lesa explicitly describes her coconut-milk prawns as a rundown-inspired preparation. “Inspired by” must remain visible.

entries.name: Fried sprat
entries.note: Xavier Murphy publishes fried sprat with seasoning. The archive’s ingredients and timing remain untested.

entries.name: Cornmeal pudding
entries.note: Grace publishes cornmeal pudding with a separately prepared soft top. Do not merge its ingredients with another pudding without identifying the adaptation.

entries.name: Coconut drops
entries.note: Grace documents diced-coconut drops with sugar and ginger. The page labels them dessert and gives a batch yield; its automatic person count should not be treated as a tested serving.

steps: Boil the water with the diced coconut for about forty minutes.
Add sugar and ginger. Continue boiling until syrupy; Grace gives about thirty to thirty-five minutes for this stage.
Spoon tablespoon portions onto a wet cookie sheet, one of the surfaces Grace specifies. Leave them to cool and set.
publishedPreparation.status: Documented source transcription; not kitchen-tested by Tony’s Guide
publishedPreparation.treatment: Source ingredient quantities preserved; directions paraphrased. No conversions or substitutions.
publishedPreparation.limitation: The source does not specify the ginger’s cut. Its stated yield is twelve drops; the automatic “one person” header is not used as a serving claim.

entries.name: Tamarind balls
entries.note: Xavier Murphy publishes tamarind balls, including an optional rum addition. The source’s preservation suggestion is not treated as a validated shelf-life claim.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 150 g brown sugar plus extra for rolling

entries.name: Soursop juice
entries.note: Lesa publishes a lime-based soursop drink and discusses other versions. Do not collapse milk-based and lime-based drinks into one fixed formula.

entries.name: Mint tea
entries.note: Jamaican producer Tops documents kitchen mint and supplies teabag brewing instructions. That does not validate the archived fresh-mint quantities or establish that all “mint” plants are interchangeable.

entries.name: Ackee and corned pork
entries.note: Grace publishes ackee and corned pork, but its method mentions garlic and escallion not listed in its ingredients. The displayed single-person yield is also questionable. Source clarification is required.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 250 g fully cooked corned pork, diced

entries.name: Salt mackerel with boiled food
entries.note: Xavier Murphy publishes salt mackerel and names boiled food as an accompaniment. Salt mackerel is not the same ingredient as fresh mackerel.

entries.name: Roast breadfruit with saltfish
entries.note: Roast breadfruit is documented, but the inspected roasting source serves it with callaloo or ackee. This does not establish the precise archived saltfish pairing formula.

entries.name: Coconut drops breakfast variation
entries.note: The underlying coconut sweet is documented. No inspected source establishes “coconut drops breakfast variation” as a distinct traditional preparation. Retain as an editorial label only.

entries.name: Cassava bammy
entries.note: This is an overlapping name for the bammy record. The same cassava-processing uncertainty applies; it is not a second authenticated tradition.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 500 g commercially processed food-safe cassava meal

entries.name: Johnny cakes
entries.note: Johnny cakes is a documented name for Jamaican fried dumplings. Keep the alias rather than treating this as an independently authenticated bread tradition.

entries.name: Coco bread
entries.note: Tanya Harris documents folded coco bread from her Jamaican household experience. A different candidate page used cocoa powder in a loaf and was rejected as the reference for this pocket bread.

entries.name: Hard dough bread
entries.note: Chef Sian Rose supplies a hardough-bread recipe and working instructions. Her published method should retain her name and its own proportions.

entries.name: Bulla cake
entries.note: Grace “Grandma” Reynolds publishes ginger bulla. No universal village or parish formula is inferred.

entries.name: Easter bun
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham’s Easter bun uses stout and dried fruit. Different bun leavening and alcohol choices require separate attribution.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 200 ml stout or nonalcoholic malt drink

entries.name: Spiced bun and cheese
entries.note: Kerri-Ann’s Kravings documents Easter bun served with cheese. This is a serving combination of the bun family, not an additional historically independent recipe.

entries.name: Jackass corn
entries.note: Winsome Murphy publishes a coconut biscuit called jackass corn. The name does not imply cornmeal is an ingredient in that published version.

entries.name: Turn cornmeal
entries.note: Chef Sian Rose documents turn cornmeal with corned pork and relates it to her western-Jamaica childhood. That is her identified experience, not a parish-wide survey.

entries.name: Cornmeal cou-cou
entries.note: Charla explicitly labels the linked okra-and-pimiento cou-cou recipe Trinidadian and distinguishes Jamaican turn cornmeal. Preserve the comparison; do not label the source formula Jamaican.

entries.name: Jerk pork
entries.note: Xavier Murphy documents jerk pork using a separate jerk sauce. The sauce and cooking method must be sourced together before a complete local formula is reconstructed.

entries.name: Oxtail and broad beans
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham publishes braised oxtail and broad beans. Keep the named bean and slow-braising preparation attached to this cook.

entries.name: Pepper steak
entries.note: Lesa publishes Jamaican-style pepper steak. This supports contemporary culinary practice, not a dated account of Chinese-Jamaican recipe invention.

entries.name: Brown stew pork
entries.note: A Jamaican food roundup identifies stew pork but does not give its own complete pork formula. It also contains a conflicting indenture chronology; do not use it as historical authority.

entries.name: Gungo peas soup
entries.note: Grace publishes a gungo-peas soup using canned peas, coconut milk and soup mix. A dried-pea or ham-bone version needs its own instructions.

ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Grace Caribbean Traditions black pepper
steps: Peel and dice the potatoes and cho-cho; set them in two cups of the water. Bring the remaining four cups to a boil and add the diced vegetables.
Stir in coconut milk, escallion, thyme, pimento, soup mix, salt and black pepper. Simmer until the potatoes and cho-cho are tender.
Drain the canned peas. Add them with the carrots, reduce the heat and simmer until the soup thickens. Serve hot.
publishedPreparation.status: Documented source transcription; not kitchen-tested by Tony’s Guide
publishedPreparation.treatment: Source ingredient quantities preserved; directions paraphrased. No conversions or substitutions.
publishedPreparation.limitation: The source does not state whether the two cups holding the diced vegetables are added to the pot. That ambiguity is retained here for clarification; no invented liquid adjustment is supplied. Product packet and can weights are not specified.

entries.name: Chicken foot soup
entries.note: Xavier Murphy documents chicken-foot soup with vegetables and ground provisions. The existence of the dish does not certify the archive’s cooking time.

entries.name: Red peas soup
entries.note: Grace’s red-peas soup uses a ham bone and ground provisions. This is a specific published variation, not a vegetarian formula.

entries.name: Mannish water
entries.note: Grace documents mannish water with goat head and belly. Do not equate any goat-meat broth with this preparation or repeat aphrodisiac claims as fact.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 1 kg cleaned goat meat with bones

entries.name: Fish tea
entries.note: Lesa publishes fish tea and separately discusses optional dumplings. Her stated personal omission is a variation, not evidence that dumplings are forbidden.

entries.name: Saturday soup
entries.note: Grace publishes Saturday Soup/Beef Soup. “Saturday soup” describes a practice as well as a dish family; chicken and beef versions need separate provenance.

entries.name: Pepperpot soup
entries.note: Winsome Murphy publishes Jamaican pepperpot and explicitly discusses a meatless option. The Jamaican recipe should not be conflated with Guyanese pepperpot.

entries.name: Cow foot stew
entries.note: Grace publishes cow foot with broad beans and pressure-cooker instructions. The source does not validate the archived stovetop duration.

entries.name: Tripe and beans
entries.note: Grace publishes curried tripe with beans and coconut milk. Curry is a source-specific feature and must not be silently omitted when attributing this version.

entries.name: Curried chickpeas
entries.note: Lesa explicitly calls her chickpea curry a Jamaican-and-Indian fusion. It can be included as a contemporary adaptation with that attribution.

entries.name: Ital stew
entries.note: Charla’s Ital vegetable stew is also used for the earlier Ital vegetable stew record. This is an overlapping dish family rather than an additional authenticated tradition.

entries.name: Ital vegetable rundown
entries.note: Original Flava describes its Ital rundown as inspired by Rastafari cooks encountered in Jamaica. It is their published interpretation, not testimony representing all Rastafari practice.

entries.name: Steamed cabbage and carrots
entries.note: Lesa’s steamed-cabbage recipe includes carrots. This overlaps the breakfast cabbage record; the serving label does not create another culinary lineage.

entries.name: Ackee and callaloo
entries.note: A blog publishes ackee, callaloo and pumpkin, but the individual cook’s identity and Jamaican provenance have not been established. Treat it as a research lead, not an authenticated Jamaican formula.

entries.name: Brown stew fish
entries.note: Lesa documents brown-stew fish, distinguishing it from steamed fish. The species, frying and sauce quantities belong to the published version.

entries.name: Saltfish rundown
entries.note: Lesa separately publishes saltfish rundown. Preserve the distinction from salted-mackerel rundown and keep her coconut-reduction method attached to her recipe.

entries.name: Pickled herring
entries.note: Winsome Murphy documents Solomon-a-Gundy, a pâté of smoked red herring. This does not authenticate the archived vinegar-pickled herring fillets; they are different preparations.

entries.name: Steamed parrotfish
entries.note: Lesa explicitly identifies parrotfish as a fish she uses for steaming and supplies a steamed-fish preparation. This is culinary documentation, not advice about current catch regulations or conservation.

entries.name: Garlic lobster
entries.note: Yanikie Tucker publishes broiled lobster tails, but that inspected recipe has no garlic. It cannot authenticate a “garlic lobster” formula.

entries.name: Crayfish rundown
entries.note: Winsome Murphy documents janga soup. A crayfish soup is not evidence for the archived crayfish rundown; that precise preparation remains unestablished in the checked material.

entries.name: Fish escovitch with bammy
entries.note: Grace explicitly pairs escovitch fish with bammy or festival. Keep this as a meal combination tied to the escovitch record, not a separate origin story.

entries.name: Saltfish buljol
entries.note: The inspected Jamaican source is pick-up saltfish. It does not authenticate the archived buljol preparation or justify labelling a wider-Caribbean name exclusively Jamaican.

entries.name: Gizzada
entries.note: Grace’s gizzada page provides pastry quantities and mentions coconut filling without a filling formula. It establishes the dish but is incomplete as a standalone recipe.

entries.name: Grater cake
entries.note: Grace documents a pink-topped grated-coconut sweet. This is distinct from the diced coconut used in drops.

entries.name: Peanut drops
entries.note: Lesa documents peanut drops with ginger and sugar. Do not substitute this evidence for coconut drops; the nut allergen remains relevant.

entries.name: Plantain tart
entries.note: Winsome Murphy publishes plantain tarts with separate pastry and filling sections. This is a named published preparation, not an authenticated match for the archive.

entries.name: Sweet potato pone
entries.note: Grace publishes a sweet-potato pone with optional yam and both fire and oven methods. It differs from the pudding source; preserve rather than erase that variation.

entries.name: Cassava pone
entries.note: Grace publishes cassava pone with sweet potato, but its method mentions unquantified vanilla. Cassava variety and safe processing still need independent validation.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 700 g commercially processed food-safe grated cassava

entries.name: Asham
entries.note: Charla publishes a modern asham preparation and describes the older parching-and-pounding practice. Her kitchen method is not an unchanged historical transcript.

entries.name: Blue draws (duckunoo)
entries.note: Grace publishes a banana-leaf-wrapped cornmeal duckunoo with optional raisins and orange sauce. It does not establish that every blue-draws version uses the same starch.

entries.name: Toto cake
entries.note: Grace “Grandma” Reynolds publishes coconut toto. The recipe is documented; its accompanying slavery-era origin story lacks the historical evidence needed for repetition as fact.

entries.name: Black cake
entries.note: Chef Sian Rose attributes this black cake to her mother’s family recipe. The claimed generations are her testimony, not independently verified genealogy.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 200 ml dark rum or fruit juice

entries.name: Rum cake
entries.note: Miss G publishes a fruit-based rum/Christmas cake. This overlaps black cake; it does not stand for every plain rum-soaked sponge sold as “rum cake”.

entries.name: Guava cheese
entries.note: The inspected guava-cheese account concerns Nevis and the wider Caribbean. It is comparative evidence, not proof of a Jamaican preparation or of the archived formula.

entries.name: Irish moss drink
entries.note: Winsome Murphy publishes an Irish-moss drink. The source’s medicinal or stamina associations are not verified health effects and are not adopted here.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 40 g commercially cleaned dried edible sea moss

entries.name: Carrot juice Jamaican style
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham’s carrot drink contains Guinness and milk-based products. Label the alcohol and dairy; a non-alcoholic version needs separate attribution.

entries.name: Peanut punch
entries.note: Lesa publishes peanut punch and distinguishes adult and child-friendly versions. Alcohol and dairy choices belong to the selected version, not an assumed single recipe.

entries.name: June plum juice
entries.note: Chef Noel Cunningham publishes a June-plum and ginger drink. It establishes his preparation without validating the archive’s fruit-to-water ratio.

entries.name: Tamarind juice
entries.note: Lesa publishes tamarind drink. Seed removal and dilution belong to her documented preparation; no medicinal claims are adopted.

entries.name: Coconut water
entries.note: Jamaica’s Scientific Research Council documents coconut-water processing work. Coconut water is an ingredient or beverage, not a compound recipe authenticated by that account.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 2 to 3 fresh drinking coconuts with approximately 1 L clear water total

entries.name: Mauby
entries.note: Cynthia Nelson’s mauby account documents her family’s wider-Caribbean practice in a Guyanese publication. It does not establish a Jamaican recipe; do not import that identity.
archivedFormulaFingerprint: 30 g commercially sold edible mauby bark

entries.name: Cerasee tea
entries.note: Jamaican producer Tops publishes cerasee teabag directions. This supports a commercial infusion, not the archived fresh-vine formula or any treatment claim.

entries.name: Guava jam
entries.note: JamaicanBikkle publishes a guava-jam formula and family anecdote but does not identify the cook on the inspected page. Attribution and a validated storage process remain outstanding.

entries.name: June plum chutney
entries.note: A 2007 Gleaner June-plum article and a PBC Jamaica chutney video were located, but the article failed to decode and the full broadcast was not inspected. No recipe authentication is claimed.

entries.name: Pepper sauce
entries.note: King’s Jamaican publishes a refrigerated pepper sauce. It supplies no validated shelf-stable canning process; the archived bottle-storage formula remains withheld.
